senses.definition: To be in opposition; to contest; to dispute; to vie; to quarrel; to fight.
senses.example: The Lord said unto me, Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle.

senses.definition: To struggle or exert oneself to obtain or retain possession of, or to defend.
senses.example:
17th century, John Dryden, Epistle III to the Lady Castlemain
You sit above, and see vain men below / Contend for what you only can bestow.

senses.definition: To be in debate; to engage in discussion; to dispute; to argue.
senses.example: these simple ideas are far from those innate principles which some contend for

senses.definition: To believe (something is reasonable) and argue (for it); to advocate.
senses.example: In this paper the author contends that no useful results can be obtained if this method is used.

senses.definition: To try to cope with a difficulty or problem.
senses.example: However, the challenges for the railway world are much greater than for automotive as we generally have more occupants, higher speeds, greater masses, higher energies, and an absence of seatbelts or airbags to contend with.
